surface_summary: Madeleine Van Norman is found stabbed in her library with a Venetian dagger and a note suggesting suicide. The house is locked and secure, and suspicion falls on her fiancé Schuyler Carleton, but inconsistencies in evidence and testimonies raise doubts.
accepted_facts: Madeleine Van Norman was found dead with a dagger wound in the library.
A written note implying suicide was found but later proven to be written by Cicely Dupuy.
The house was securely locked with no signs of forced entry except the front door with a latch-key.
Schuyler Carleton entered the house shortly before the alarm was raised.
inferred_conclusions: Madeleine killed herself due to unhappiness over her fiancé's lack of love.
Schuyler Carleton murdered Madeleine out of jealousy and love for another woman.
The murderer was an outside burglar who entered through a window.
mechanism_description: Tom Willard entered the house through a cellar window and climbed up the ash-chute in the drawing-room fireplace to the library. There, in a fit of rage during a quarrel with Madeleine, he stabbed her with the Venetian dagger. He then left the same way, leaving the house locked and undisturbed. The note was a forgery by Cicely Dupuy to suggest suicide.
delivery_path: Tom Willard leaves the Van Norman house at 10 pm to stay at the Mapleton Inn.
He returns secretly by climbing through the cellar window and ascending the ash-chute in the fireplace.
Tom confronts Madeleine in the library and quarrels with her about her engagement.
In a sudden rage, Tom stabs Madeleine with the Venetian dagger, killing her instantly.
He drops the dagger and leaves the room, descending back through the ash-chute and cellar window.
Schuyler Carleton arrives at the house at 11:15 pm, unaware of the murder until he finds Madeleine.
Cicely Dupuy writes a false note to suggest suicide and later attempts to retrieve it.
outcome_result: Tom Willard confesses to the murder and dies from a self-inflicted wound.

false_assumption.statement: The note found on the table was a dying confession written by Madeleine Van Norman herself.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The note was in handwriting very similar to Madeleine's and was found beside her body, suggesting she wrote it just before dying. The presence of the note and the nature of the wound led many to believe it was a suicide.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The note was actually written by Cicely Dupuy days earlier and planted to mislead investigators. This false assumption obscured the fact that Madeleine was murdered by another person.

supporting_points: He was the fiancé and had a motive related to love and jealousy.
He entered the house shortly before the alarm was raised.
He refused to disclose his errand or activities during the critical time.
His demeanor was nervous and evasive during questioning.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He had a credible alibi for the time of the murder and no physical evidence linked him to the crime scene.

red_herrings.description: Cicely Dupuy wrote the false note and showed suspicious behavior, including fainting and evasiveness.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Her actions stemmed from her secret love for Carleton and fear of incriminating him, not guilt in the murder.

red_herrings.description: Miss Morton secretly burned papers found in Madeleine's desk, raising suspicions about her motives.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: She burned old letters related to a past quarrel with Richard Van Norman and not any evidence related to the murder.

closed_circle.rationale: The murder had to be committed by someone inside the locked house during a narrow time window, limiting suspects to household members and guests present.

time_windows: Between 10:30 pm and 11:30 pm murder occurs

inference_path.observation: The note was written with a soft pencil unlike the hard pencil on the library table.
inference_path.correction: The note was not written at the library table on the night of the murder.
inference_path.effect: The note's status as a dying confession is questioned.
required_evidence: The soft pencil found in Cicely Dupuy's desk
Handwriting comparison between note and Cicely Dupuy's writing

inference_path.observation: No blood stains on Madeleine's right hand despite blood on dagger handle.
inference_path.correction: Madeleine could not have held the dagger when it was stained with blood.
inference_path.effect: The theory of suicide is undermined.
required_evidence: Examination of Madeleine's hands for blood stains
Examination of dagger for blood stains

inference_path.observation: Schuyler Carleton entered the house at 11:15 pm but called for help at 11:30 pm.
inference_path.correction: There is a 15-minute unexplained interval in Carleton's timeline.
inference_path.effect: Suspicion falls on Carleton due to unexplained time gap.
required_evidence: Mr. Hunt's testimony about time of Carleton's entry
Carleton's own testimony about time of entry and alarm

inference_path.observation: A cachou was found on the drawing-room floor, uncommon in Mapleton.
inference_path.correction: The cachou likely dropped by the murderer during entry or exit.
inference_path.effect: Links Tom Willard to the crime scene as he possessed such cachous.
required_evidence: Testimony of Mapleton Inn landlord about cachous found in Willard's room
Location of cachou found in Van Norman house

inference_path.observation: The house was securely locked with bolts and no forced entry signs.
inference_path.correction: The murderer must have entered and exited through an unconventional route.
inference_path.effect: Focus shifts to cellar window and ash-chute as entry/exit points.
required_evidence: Butler Harris's testimony about locks and bolts
Fleming Stone's discovery of ash-chute opening in fireplace

inference_path.observation: The ash-chute opening is only 9.5 by 13.5 inches, seemingly too small for a large man.
inference_path.correction: An experienced engineer like Tom Willard could squeeze through it.
inference_path.effect: Tom Willard's physical ability and occupation make him a plausible suspect.
required_evidence: Testimony about Tom Willard's engineering experience

inference_path.observation: Tom Willard confessed to the murder and then fatally wounded himself.
inference_path.correction: The confession confirms the true mechanism and identity of the murderer.
inference_path.effect: Case is solved with Tom Willard as the culprit.
required_evidence: Tom Willard's confession at the Van Norman house
Medical confirmation of Tom Willard's fatal wound

discriminating_test.design: Fleming Stone examined the locked house and discovered the ash-chute in the fireplace as a secret entry and exit route. He measured the opening and confirmed that only someone with Tom Willard's engineering skills could have used it. The presence of a rare cachou in the drawing-room linked the suspect to the scene. This physical constraint proof eliminated other suspects who lacked access or ability.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The murderer entered and exited through the cellar window and ash-chute, bypassing locked doors and windows, proving the impossibility of other suspects' involvement.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Verification that the ash-chute opening matches the physical capability of the suspect and that no other entry was possible.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given all necessary clues: the note's handwriting and pencil discrepancy, the absence of blood on the victim's hands, the locked house with no forced entry, the testimony about the time of entry and alarm, the discovery of the cachou, and the ash-chute as a secret passage. The suspect's occupation and physical ability are also revealed. These facts allow the attentive reader to deduce the true murderer before the confession.
